description: [phase 3.8 38g, kind `scope`] showRoutingMapScreen exit: each golfer hole byte above 0 is replaced by entry [byte] of a 20-dword table on the stack; a byte of 20 or more reads the dwords above that table (the return address and the caller frame, 0x004586e8 / 0x004586ef). The port does not model the caller frame: with the defect switch showRoutingMapScreen.exitRemapReadsFrame ON (default, the original) it throws MissingResource for such a byte, OFF it leaves the byte alone. A game state holds hole bytes 0..19 (record 19 is the leaving slot), so only a corrupt state reaches it; the oracle compares OFF against the original with those bytes masked.

[phase 3.8 38g, kind `oracle`] The redraw calls slot 0x9c of the live display object (0x00456c54, 0x00456ce6, 0x00457faf, 0x004586b5) and writes the drawing scratch words g_linePoint (setLinePoint / lineTo) and g_map822b80[1] (the last cell pointer, 0x00456e5c, 0x0045776c, 0x00457915, 0x00457abe). The port drops all of them; the oracle stubs the slot, the drawing callees and cellAt with routines that write nothing and masks those two words, so it proves the exe-side simulation writes only. rateLot, evalPlacementArea and sampleHeight (value helpers of the mode 2 and height colouring) are stubbed too: their notes list stack writes only, so the port does not call them.

[phase 3.8 38g, kind `oracle`] The scroll-up arrow with a scrolled list (state 9 and scroll > 0: 0x00458353 / 0x0045835b) and a down arrow with no hidden walker left (0x00458363) need the hovered button to change between two passes. The oracle and QueueInput give every cursor read the same point, so those three branch sides are not reached by it; segments with a trace cursor sequence reach them. The port body is a direct transcription of the rest of the loop.

[phase 3.8 38g, kind `scope`] showMembershipRoster clears bit 7 of byte +2 of ALL 76 golfer-type records at the end of every redraw (0x00455713..0x00455728), not only the pass marker it set on the listed ones, so the exclusion bit those records carry on entry is lost after the first redraw. The row selection itself (name order, 0x230-byte names strcpy-ed into a 19-byte stack buffer at 0x00454fb6, so a name of 19 characters or more overflows it) and the scroll offset only choose the drawn rows and are not ported; the port keeps the marker clearing. The oracle runs the original over the game's own names.

[phase 3.8 38g, kind `oracle`] showShortcutsScreen and showMembershipRoster return what their last callee returns (Image_dtor 0x0044f68e, pumpLight 0x00455a03); the oracle stubs those callees and compares neither eax nor the screen's return, the port returns 0. The only caller is mainLoop's frame step (the port's tick_frame.inc calls both without using the result). The cursor-sequence branches of showMembershipRoster (a zone left for another zone sets the redraw flag, 0x00455857 / 0x004558d3 / 0x00455934) need a cursor that moves between passes, as U-1022.
